summary: Qian proves potential ordinary automorphy for n-dimensional residual representations of the Galois group of a CM field (Theorem 1.1), using an asymmetric Dwork family and a second prime. With ACC+ he deduces potential automorphy for suitable l-adic representations (Theorem 1.4). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed, and thirteen findings are recorded. Theorem 1.4 is established only for l > n, since the lifting theorem it uses requires p > n (E2); Lemma 3.12 needs v(t) < 0 (E1). Not formalised.

items.name: Continuous residual representation and residual semisimplification
items.statement: A residual representation is a continuous homomorphism G_F→GL_n(k) for a finite field k of characteristic l, with discrete target. For an l-adic representation choose a stable lattice over a finite coefficient extension and semisimplify its reduction; the resulting representation over F_l-bar is independent of the lattice up to isomorphism. A bar on r throughout Theorem 1.4 denotes this residual representation, not r itself.

items.name: Regular ordinary local Galois representation
items.statement: For a p-adic local field K, a continuous rho:G_K→GL_n(Q_p-bar) is ordinary of regular weight lambda if lambda_(tau,1)≥...≥lambda_(tau,n) are integers for every tau:K→Q_p-bar and rho has an invariant full flag with one-dimensional graded characters psi_i. On an open subgroup of inertia, psi_i(sigma)=∏_tau tau(Art_K^(-1)(sigma))^(-(lambda_(tau,n-i+1)+i-1)). This is a condition on the actual flag and inertia characters; potential semistability is separately required by the lifting theorem.

items.name: Enormous residual image
items.statement: For an algebraic extension k/F_p and absolutely irreducible H⊂GL_n(k), put ad0=ker(tr:End_k(k^n)→k) with conjugation action. This condition is not merely adequacy, and is impossible when p divides n.

items.name: Residual potential ordinary automorphy
items.statement: Let F be a CM number field, F_av/F finite, n≥2, l an odd prime, s≥1, and rbar:G_F→GL_n(F_(l^s)) continuous and semisimple. There is a finite CM extension F'/F which is Galois and linearly disjoint from F_av over F, such that rbar|G_F' is ordinarily automorphic. No residual irreducibility, polarization, regularity or enormous-image hypothesis is imposed here.

items.proofOutline: Choose the asymmetric Dwork family and coefficient primes, match both determinants by roots over controlled fields, use Moret–Bailly to obtain the switching point, lift the auxiliary automorphic seed, transfer coefficients, then invoke the published Steinberg ordinary bridge and untwist. items.name: Potential automorphy of a supplied ordinary lift: supported range
items.statement: Let F be CM, F_av/F finite, n≥2, l odd with l>n, iota:Q_l-bar≅C, and r:G_F→GL_n(Q_l-bar) continuous, unramified outside finitely many places, and potentially semistable regular ordinary at every v|l. Suppose rbar is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, rbar(G_F(zeta_l)) is enormous, and some sigma∈G_F\G_F(zeta_l) has scalar rbar(sigma). Then some finite CM Galois F'/F, linearly disjoint from F_av/F, makes r|G_F' iota-ordinarily automorphic. The extra l>n is the verified hypothesis of ACC+ 6.1.2(4); Qian prints the wider odd-l assertion, whose remaining range is an explicit unresolved proof gate, not certified here.

items.name: Finite support and local killing of a root obstruction
items.statement: A class in H^2(G_M,Z/m) is inflated from a finite Galois quotient and has zero localization at every finite place unramified in that quotient, since H^2 of the procyclic unramified quotient with finite discrete coefficients vanishes. After adjoining mu_m locally, the local invariant identifies H^2(K,mu_m) with (1/m)Z/Z; restriction through a finite extension multiplies the invariant by the extension degree. Thus degrees divisible by m kill the local class.

The order-at-most-two computation therefore gives Cor(Sha^1(L,mu_m))=0, hence Res(Sha^2(K,Z/m))=0 by item020. Lemma 2.1 constructs such an L using a totally real Galois auxiliary field while preserving the prescribed avoidance.

uses.how: Input to Roots of finite-field-valued characters with avoidance.

items.proofOutline: Use disjointness to identify the finite cyclotomic Galois groups under restriction, then CorRes=[L:K]; its even degree kills the at-most-two group. Duality makes the corresponding Sha2 restriction zero.

items.name: Auxiliary modulus with prescribed order and nonunitary condition

The construction uses pairwise coprime factors with orders high powers of the prime divisors of s, including a two-prime factor of 2-power order. By also excluding all primes below a chosen bound, N can be forced above that bound.

items.name: Crystalline slope criterion for regular ordinarity
items.statement: Let r:G_F→GL_n(Q_l-bar) be crystalline at every v|l. For a_tau,1≥...≥a_tau,n, assume gr^i D_dR,tau(r) has dimension one for i=a_tau,j+n−j and zero otherwise. Let alpha_v,1,...,alpha_v,n be the eigenvalues of phi^[F_v^0:Q_l] on D_cris,tau(r), ordered by decreasing val_v, where val_v(l)=v(l) for the integral valuation v on F_v. Then r is ordinary of weight a iff val_v(alpha_v,i)=∑_(tau above v)(a_tau,i+n−i) for every v and i. All embeddings above v enter the sum.

Prove the Gauss determinant formula and prime-specific n-th-power matching, the consecutive labelled Hodge weights, crystallinity at good fibres, ordinary behavior near t=0 when l≡1 modN, and maximal away-from-l monodromy only at v(t)<0. The controlled-point output is item081: prescribed two twisted residual realizations at a CM Galois extension, original-prime negative valuations, auxiliary-prime positive valuations, and precisely based avoidance intersections.
